title: Good Friday Agreement
description:
The **Good Friday Agreement**, also known as the Belfast Agreement, was signed on April 10, 1998, marking a major political development in the Northern Ireland peace process.

The agreement established a framework for devolved government in Northern Ireland and created new institutions linking Northern Ireland, the Republic of Ireland, and the United Kingdom. It addressed issues of governance, human rights, policing, and decommissioning of paramilitary weapons.

The agreement was approved by referendum in both Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland. It largely ended the period known as "the Troubles," a 30-year conflict that claimed over 3,500 lives. The architects of the agreement, John Hume and David Trimble, were awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1998.
